revision.text:
{{documentation}} {{invokes|Infotable Bonuses}} Template for inserting a table of item bonuses on a page. This lists a number of equippable game items, that has some kind of relation to each other, along with their associated stats in a table layout for an easy overview. This could be items that are part of an armour set or items that fall into the same category. Pages this template is suitable for is disambiguation pages for item categories, and also for pages dedicated to an armour set. It can also be useful for item pages where its desireable to compare an item against other similar items, although the latter should probably be reserved for top-tier items. This template is ''not'' suitable for comparing weapons though, but it can nevertheless be used on disambiguation pages for weapons to provide an overview. ==Usage== {{T|Infotable Bonuses|item1|item2|item3 ...}} Items listed needs to match the name of a wiki page that uses [[Template:Infobox Bonuses]]. In case an item has multiple variants, one of the subvariants has to be specified by appending a '#' sign and the sub-variant's name. If you are unsure as to which variant to list, you can use the base name of the item and turn off sorting temporary, this should present you with a list of variants to chose from. The one you want is ususally the undamaged item or otherwise the item with the highest stats. For items that can be charged, you can pick the uncharged version if the stats are the same, otherwise chose the charged one. Pages which erroneously lists multi-variant items will be added to [[:Category:Infotable Bonuses with multi-variant items]] allowing maintainers to find and fix lists with errors in them. ==Examples== {{T|Infotable Bonuses|Verac's brassard#Undamaged|Verac's flail#Undamaged|Verac's helm#Undamaged|Verac's plateskirt#Undamaged}} {{Infotable Bonuses|Verac's brassard#Undamaged|Verac's flail#Undamaged|Verac's helm#Undamaged|Verac's plateskirt#Undamaged}} {{T|Infotable Bonuses|Bronze axe|Iron axe|Steel axe|Black axe|Mithril axe|Adamant axe|Rune axe|Dragon axe|Crystal axe#Active|nototals=yes|sort=str|order=asc|attackspeed=yes}} {{Infotable Bonuses|Bronze axe|Iron axe|Steel axe|Black axe|Mithril axe|Adamant axe|Rune axe|Dragon axe|Crystal axe#Active|nototals=yes|sort=str|order=asc|attackspeed=yes}} ===Split totals=== {{T|Infotable Bonuses|Lunar helm|Lunar torso|Lunar legs|Lunar gloves|Lunar boots|Lunar cape|itemwidth=110px|colwidth=30px}} {{T|Infotable Bonuses|Lunar amulet|Lunar ring|Lunar staff|itemwidth=110px|colwidth=30px|noheader=yes}} {{Infotable Bonuses|Lunar helm|Lunar torso|Lunar legs|Lunar gloves|Lunar boots|Lunar cape|itemwidth=110px|colwidth=42px}} {{Infotable Bonuses|Lunar amulet|Lunar ring|Lunar staff|itemwidth=110px|colwidth=42px|noheader=yes}} ===Row comments=== Useful when using the infotable for a tier comparison of a single equipment slot, and commentary per item is helpful. 
{{Infotable Bonuses|sort=dslash
|Leather gloves |comment1 = Although their crush defence bonus is better than that of [[leather vambraces]], the difference is minimal - and slash attack type is significantly more common due to scimitars and 2-handed swords.
|Leather vambraces |comment2 = Considered the best free-to-play gloves without any level requirements. Since they have no attack penalties, mages can safely use these gloves and are encouraged to do so.
|Green d'hide vambraces |comment3 = The best gloves available for both ranged and melee combat.
}}
{{Infotable Bonuses|sort=dslash |Leather gloves |comment1 = Although their crush defence bonus is better than that of [[leather vambraces]], the difference is minimal - and slash attack type is significantly more common due to scimitars and 2-handed swords. |Leather vambraces |comment2 = Considered the best free-to-play gloves without any level requirements. Since they have no attack penalties, mages can safely use these gloves and are encouraged to do so. |Green d'hide vambraces |comment3 = The best gloves available for both ranged and melee combat. }} ==Parameters== ===Numbered parameters=== {| !style="text-align:left" | Parameter !style="text-align:left; width:100%" | Description !style="text-align:left" | Default !style="text-align:left" | Required |- |item1, item2, item3 ... || Items to list. Items listed needs to match the name of a wiki page that uses [[Template:Infobox Bonuses]]. In case an item has multiple variants, one of the subvariants has to be specified by appending a '#' sign and the sub-variant's name. || {{NA}} || required |- |} Pages which erroneously lists multi-variant items will be added to [[:Category:Infotable Bonuses with multi-variant items]] allowing maintainers to find and fix lists with errors in them. ;Filters Providing a page name containing two colons will use that as a filter instead; e.g. {{Infotable Bonuses|combat_style::Polearm}} will instead search for combat_style = Polearm in the infobox bonuses bucket ([https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Special:Bucket?bucket=infobox_bonuses&select=*&where=%7Bcombat_style%3D%27Polearm%27%7D&limit=20&offset=0]). However, this will throw Lua errors if you don't include sort and nototals arguments (ex. {{Infotable Bonuses|combat_style::Polearm|sort=acrush|nototals=yes}}) ===Named parameters=== {| !style="text-align:left" | Parameter !style="text-align:left; width:100%" | Description !style="text-align:left" | Default !style="text-align:left" | Required |- | comment''1''
comment''N'' || Comment for the respective item at index ''1'' through ''N''. If no comments are specified, the comments column is not shown. || {{NA}} || optional |- | noheader || Set to 'yes' to omit table header. || 'no' || optional |- | nototals || Set to 'yes' to omit totals. || 'no' || optional |- | sort || Sorting key. Set to one or more of: 'astab', 'aslash', 'acrush', 'amagic', 'arange', 'dstab', 'dslash', 'dcrush', 'dmagic', 'drange', 'str', 'mdmg', 'rstr' and 'prayer'. Use comma as a separator between the sorting keys. || (alphabetical) || optional |- | order || Sorting order. Set to one or more of: 'ascending', 'asc', 'descending', 'desc', 'reverse', 'random' and 'rand'. Use comma as a separator between the sorting orders. || 'ascending' || optional |- | colwidth || Default column width intended for the split-totals mode. || {{NA}} || optional |- | itemwidth || Default item column width intended for the split-totals mode. || {{NA}} || optional |- | expensive || Exists only to help maintainers locate errors on wiki pages, and can be enabled site-wide by changing a default in the Lua module. Should be disabled unless doing maintenance. || false || optional, debug |- | attackspeed || Include a column with the attack speed of each item |- | attackrange || Include a column with the attack range of each item |- |} ==See also== * [[Template:Infobox Bonuses]] * [[Template:Slottable]] [[Category:Lua-based templates|{{PAGENAME}}]]

{{Documentation}} {{Invokes|Instructions}} ==About== This template is used in conjunction with [[Template:Recipe]] to create a list of instructions on how to create a specific item. This can be used for anything, but it was built specifically for a subsection under the recipe template. ==Usage== 
{{Instructions

}}

{{Instructions
|step1 = Find the bacon.

|step3 = Cry for lack of bacon.

}}

{{documentation}} This template provides basic formatting to display an inventory. ==Usage== This template can be used by entering the following onto a relevant page. 
{{Inventory|align=right
|Item1 |Item2 |Item3 |Item4
|Item5 |Item6 |Item7 |Item8
|Item9 |Item10 |Item11 |Item12
|Item13 |Item14 |Item15 |Item16
|Item17 |Item18 |Item19 |Item20
|Item21 |Item22 |Item23 |Item24
|Item25 |Item26 |Item27 |Item28
}}
To specify an amount for a stackable item, put a backslash and insert the amount after the backslash. To align the inventory to a specific side, use the ''align'' parameter. For example, use |align=right to move the table to the right of the page. To switch to a horizontal table, use |orient=h. If an item is noted, add ;n at the end of the item line. If an item has a different in-game name than the #anchor link required for the article, add ;Itemname#Anchor after the item name. This can be used together with the above ;n flag and item amounts, if necessary. ==Examples== If you want to suggest an inventory for [[Ectofuntus]] trips, you could do the following: {{Inventory|align=right |Ectophial | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |Bones |Bones |Bones |Bones |Bones |Bones |Bones |Bones |Bones }} 
{{Inventory|align=right
|Ectophial | | |
| | | |
| | | |
| | | |
| | | |Bones
|Bones |Bones |Bones |Bones
|Bones |Bones |Bones |Bones
}}
{{clear}} ;Quantity To specify an amount, use a backslash and enter the amount for that item. For example: {{Inventory|align=right|orient=h |Steel cannonball\12 | | |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar }} 
{{Inventory|align=right|orient=h
|Steel cannonball\12 | | |Steel bar
|Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar
|Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar
|Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar
|Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar
|Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar
|Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar |Steel bar
}}
{{clear}} ;Noted To mark an item as noted, add ;n after the item name. Can be combined with quantity (in either order). {{Inventory|align=right |Shark;n | | | | | |Magic logs;n\100 | | | | | |Runite ore\50;n | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | }} 
{{Inventory|align=right
|Shark;n | | |
| | |Magic logs;n\100 |
| | | |
|Runite ore\50;n | | |
| | | |
| | | |
| | | |
}}

Quantity and noted flag must be appended at the end. {{Inventory|align=right |Dragon dagger(p++);Dragon dagger#Poison++ | | | | | |Divine super combat potion(2);Divine super combat potion#2 dose;n\20 | | | | | |Strange device;Strange device#Master | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | }} 
{{Inventory|align=right

| | |Divine super combat potion(2);Divine super combat potion#2 dose;n\20 |
| | | |
|Strange device;Strange device#Master | | |
| | | |
| | | |
| | | |
}}

| | | |
| | | |
| | | |

}}

revision.text:
-- 
-- Implements various currency templates
--

local p = {}

local function amount (a, coinType)
    -- convert used globals to locals where possible to improve performance
    local math = math
    local string = string
    local table = table
    local mw = mw
    local expr = mw.ext.ParserFunctions.expr

    local ret = {' '1,000'
    a = string.gsub(a, ',', '')

    -- cache tonumber result
    a2 = tonumber(a)

    -- only do this if required so as not to impact performance too much
    if a2 == nil then
        a = expr(a)
        a2 = tonumber(a) or 0
    end

    -- round to 2 d.p.
    a = math.floor(a2 * 100 + 0.5) / 100

    -- select which image class to use for css to hook off
    num = math.abs(a)
    amounts = {10000, 1000, 250, 100, 25, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1}

    for i = 1, #amounts do
        j = amounts[i]

        if num >= j then
            break
        end
    end
    ret[3] = tostring(j)
    if noCoins[coinType] then
    	ret[3] = ''
    end

    -- set a class to denote positive or negative (css sets the colour)
    if a > 0 then
        ret[4] = ' coins-pos">'
    elseif a < 0 then
        ret[4] = ' coins-neg">'
    else
        ret[4] = '">'
    end
    
    local lang = mw.language.getContentLanguage();

	-- Assumes (for now) that all currencies want at least 2 significant digits
	--   if the number has a fractional part.
    if coinType == 'fiat' then
    	-- The fractional value returned is guaranteed to be formatted as 0.X
    	local whole, frac = math.modf(num)
    	ret[5] = lang:formatNum(whole)
    	-- Concat formatted whole portion onto fractional portion, if needed
    	if frac > 0 then
    		ret[5] = ret[5] .. string.format('%.2f', frac):sub(2)
    	end
    else
    	-- format number with commas
    	ret[5] = lang:formatNum(a)
    end

    if noCoins[coinType] then
    	ret[5] = ret[5] .. noCoins[coinType]
    end

    return table.concat( ret )
end

--
-- {{Coins}}
--
function p.coins(frame)
    local args = frame:getParent().args
    -- for {{coins|111}}
    local a = args[1] or '0'
    return amount(a, 'coins')
end

function p.nocoins(frame)
    local args = frame:getParent().args
    local c = 'nocoins'
    if string.find(args[2] or '', '%S') then
    	c = 'nocoinsc'
    end
    local a = args[1] or '0'
    return amount(a, c)
end

function p.fiat(frame)
	local args = frame:getParent().args
	local a = args[1] or '0'
	return amount(a, 'fiat')
end

--
-- Module access point
--
function p._amount(a, coinType)
    a = tostring(a) or '0'
    return amount(a, coinType)
end

return p

{{Documentation}} {{invokes|Level up table}} The '''Level up table''' template is used in the various skill level-up tables (for example, [[Attack/Level up table]]) to create a table that details abilities gained with every level, both by members and by all players. These unlocks are described as for [[free-to-play]] and [[members]]. ==Usage==

|freeplayall = The abilities unlocked upon every level by both free-players and members.
|membersall  = The abilities unlocked upon every level by members only.

|members1   = The abilities unlocked with level 1 by members only.
|freeplay2  = The abilities unlocked with level 2 by both free-players and members.
|members2   = The abilities unlocked with level 2 by members only.
.
.
.
|freeplay99  = The abilities unlocked with level 99 by both free-players and members.
|members99   = The abilities unlocked with level 99 by members only.
}}

revision.text:
{{documentation}} Used to generate a table entry for object locations. Provides cells for location string, members, amount of spawns and link to map. See also [[:Template:ObjectTableHead]] and [[:Template:ObjectTableBottom]]. ==See also== This template should be used for scenery object locations. Location lists for other entities include: * {{T|LocLine}} - Used for NPC/monster spawn locations * {{T|ItemSpawnLine}} - Used for item spawns * {{T|ShopLocLine}} - Used for shop locations ==Parameters== ===Table-related=== *'''location''': location of the object. *'''members''': whether the object is member's only. Accepts yes/no. Defaults to no. *'''spawns''': amount of spawns the object has. If not defined, automatically takes number from amount of map coordinates. ===Map-related=== See [[:Template:Map]] and [[:Module:Map]] for information on mapping. *'''name''' *'''mapID''' *'''plane''' *'''icon''' *'''ptype''' *'''r''' *'''mtype''' ==Example== 
{{ObjectTableHead}}
{{ObjectLocLine
|name = Dairy churn
|location = [[Hosidius]] West of the plows
|members = Yes
|mapID = 0
|plane = 0
|x:1747,y:3536
|mtype = pin
}}
{{ObjectTableBottom}}
produces: {{ObjectTableHead}} {{ObjectLocLine |name = Dairy churn |location = [[Hosidius]] West of the plows |members = Yes |mapID = 0 |plane = 0 |x:1747,y:3536 |mtype = pin }} {{ObjectTableBottom}}

revision.comment: support for overriding symbol on all features defined in a locline
revision.text:
{{Documentation}} {{ToC|right}} The '''LocLine''' templates are used to list a monster's locations. Three templates are used to form the locations table: * {{T|LocTableHead}} - Contains table headers for the top of the locations table * {{T|LocLine}} - Template for all of the individual location lines * {{T|LocTableBottom}} - Contains table footers for the bottom of the locations table ==See also== This template should be used for NPC and Monster locations. Location lists for other entities include: * {{T|ItemSpawnLine}} - Used for item spawns * {{T|ObjectLocLine}} - Used for object/scenery locations * {{T|ShopLocLine}} - Used for shops or other places ==Usage== 
{{LocTableHead}}
{{LocLine
|name        = 
|location         = 
|levels      = 
|members     = 
|mapID       = 
|plane       = 
|(coordN)      
|mtype       = 
|icon        = 
}}
{{LocTableBottom}}
===Unfilled location lines for quick copy-paste=== 
{{LocTableHead}}
{{LocLine
|location = 
|levels = 
|members = 
|mapID = 
|plane = 
|mtype = 

}}
{{LocTableBottom}}
==Parameter details== ===name=== Optional. Name of the monster/NPC. Defaults to the title of the page on which the template is placed. Used as a title in the tooltips that appear when clicking on the pins of the interactive map. ===location=== Text, typically an article link, used to name a given location row. ===levels=== The level or levels (typically given as a comma-separated list of numbers and/or ranges) of the monster spawns at the given location. ===members=== Optional. A "yes" or "no" value indicating whether or not the given location is members-only. Defaults to "no". ===mapID=== Optional. The interactive [[RuneScape:Map/mapIDs|map ID]]. See {{T|Template:Map}} for more info. ===plane=== Optional. The inteactive map plane. See {{T|Template:Map}} for more info. ===mtype=== Semi-required. Type of map design with coordinates. (pin, circle, square, polygon) ===icon=== Optional. The symbol name to override this line's appearance on the map (e.g. bluePin, redPin, greenPin). Can be used to distinguish NPC spawns in the same location, e.g. [[Araxyte]]. ===Unnamed parameters=== One or more coordinates given as unnamed parameters. See {{T|Template:Map}} for more info. Note that both the (x,y) form (e.g. |1234,4567) and the key-value pair form (e.g. |desc:A description for the pin,x:1234,y:4567) are accepted. '''Note:''' When using the key-value pair form, passing an npcid value without specifying a pin description (via a desc value) will generate a pin description in the form of: ''NPC ID: 1234''. This mirrors the behaviour used by {{T|Monster map}} and {{T|NPC map}}.

revision.comment: add more arg doc links
revision.text:
{{documentation}} The Map template is used to easily create interactive maps or inline links to interactive maps. To find coordinates of a specific map square, use a tool such as https://mejrs.github.io/osrs. For a guide on how to manually define maps, see [[RuneScape:Create Map]]. =Map options= ===Location=== The map's centre is defined by [[#arg-map-x|x]] and [[#arg-map-y|y]] coordinates or custom features. A map with no coordinates or features will default to Lumbridge. {| class="center" ! style="width: 50svh" | Default !! style="width: 50svh" | Placed |- | {{Map}} | {{Map|x=3165|y=3494}} |- | {{Map}} | {{Map|x=3165|y=3494}} |} ===Zoom, plane and mapID=== [[#arg-map-zoom|zoom]] — Overrides the automatic calculated zoom. Higher numbers result in a greater zoom. [[#arg-feat-plane|plane]] — Sets the plane (or floor) for a specific feature (by [[RuneScape:Style_guide#Floor_numbering|British floor numbering]]). Features can be defined on different planes on the same map. [[#arg-map-mapid|mapID]] — Sets the predefined area of the [[World map]], such as a dungeon, for an entire Map instance. A list of all possible mapIDs can be found at [[RuneScape:Map/mapIDs]], with centre points for each ID. Defaults to 0, rendering only Gielinor's surface. Features on a single Map cannot span multiple mapIDs. If this is needed, use [[#Grouping|grouping]] across multiple Maps on the same page each with a different mapID. {| class="center" ! style="width: 33svh" | Zoom 0 !! style="width: 33svh" | {{Floor|uk=2}} of Lumbridge Castle !! style="width: 33svh" | [[Tolna's Rift]] |- | {{Map|zoom=0}} | {{Map|plane=2}} | {{Map|mapID=21|3104,5280}} |- | {{Map|zoom=0}} | {{Map|plane=2}} | {{Map|mapID=21|3104,5280}} |} ===Width and height=== [[#arg-map-width|width]] and [[#arg-map-height|height]] control the pixel size of a map frame. {| class="center" ! Short and Wide |- | {{Map|width=600|height=200}} |- |{{Map|width=600|height=200}} |} ===Alignment=== [[#arg-map-align|align]] changes the alignment of a map frame on a page. {| class="center" ! style="width: 33svh" | Left !! style="width: 33svh" | Center !! style="width: 33svh" | Right |- | {{Map|align=left}} | {{Map|align=center}} | {{Map|align=right}} |- | class="left" |{{Map|align=left}} | class="center" |{{Map|align=center}} | style="text-align:right" |{{Map|align=right}} |} ===Captions and legends=== A [[#arg-map-caption|caption]] can be used to describe features or show additional information relevant to a location. These can include templates made for formatting map legends/keys. {|class="center" ! style="width: 33svh" | Caption !! style="width: 33svh" | Legend !! style="width: 33svh" | Mapkey |- | |caption=Location of the entrance.}} | |caption= {{Legend|#4EF3F3|caption=Lily of the elid}} | 
|caption={{mapkey
|title = The Summer Shore
|line1 = alt...[[File:Herbalist_icon.png]],text={{chatl|Mag}} the herbalist
|line2=dot...yellow,text=[[Bank Deposit Box]]
|line3=polygon...,text=Statue}}
|- |{{Map|name=Chasm of Fire|x=1435|y=3668|zoom=2|caption=Location of the entrance for the [[Chasm of Fire]].}} |{{Map|x=3353|y=2927|mtype=pin|icon=cyanPin|caption= {{Legend|#4EF3F3|caption=Lily of the elid}}}} |{{Map|zoom=3|mtype=square|r=1|3168,2411|group=maniwashere|mtype:dot,fill:#FFFF00,3177,2420 |caption= {{mapkey |title = The Summer Shore |line1 = alt...[[File:Herbalist icon.png]],text={{chatl|Mag}} the herbalist |line2 = dot...yellow,text=[[Bank Deposit Box]] |line3 = polygon...,text=Statue }} }} |} ===Maplinks=== Any map can be rendered as a link instead of inline by setting [[#arg-map-type|type]] to maplink. With this, [[#arg-map-text|text]] is used to change the text of the link. {| class="center" |- | {{Map|type=maplink}}
{{Map|type=maplink}} | {{Map|type=maplink|text=Maplink Text}}
{{Map|type=maplink|text=Maplink Text}} |- | {{Map|type=maplink|text=}}
{{Map|type=maplink|text=}} | {{Map|type=maplink|mtype=pin|2613,3294}}
{{Map|type=maplink|mtype=pin|2613,3294|group=maplinks}} |} =Features= Map features are defined with an [[#arg-feat-mtype|mtype]] and require one or more coordinates to be valid. ==Single-point== With [[#def-single-point-feature|single-point features]], multiple coordinates will produce multiple of one type of feature. ===Pins=== Pins are commonly used to mark things that take up a 1x1 space or otherwise have an exact X/Y location. Pins have a strict set of colour values, changed by setting [[#arg-pin-icon|icon]] to either greenPin, redPin, bluePin, cyanPin, magentaPin, yellowPin or greyPin. {| class="center" ! style="width: 50svh" | Pin !! style="width: 50svh" | Magenta Pins |- | {{Map|mtype=pin|2965,3381}} | {{Map|mtype=pin|icon=magentaPin|2638,3300|2661,3308}} |- | {{Map|mtype=pin|2965,3381|group=pins}} | {{Map|mtype=pin|icon=magentaPin|2638,3300|2661,3308|group=pins2}} |} ===Dots=== Like pins, dots are also used to mark precise locations. However, dots are better suited for marking many tightly packed coordinates. {| class="center" ! Dots |- | {{Map|mtype=dot|1843,3728|1847,3728
|1851,3728 ... }} |- | {{Map|mtype=dot|1843,3728|1847,3728|1851,3728|1851,3724|1851,3720|1847,3720|1843,3720|group=dots}} |} ===Circles, squares and rectangles=== Circles and squares are defined by a centre point and a radius [[#arg-feat-r|r]]. For squares, r defines half the length of the square's edges—i.e., the shortest distance from its centre to one of its edges. Rectangles are also defined by a single point, though its side lengths are defined with [[#arg-rect-x|rectX]] and [[#arg-rect-y|rectY]]. {| class="center" ! style="width: 33svh" | Circle !! style="width: 33svh" | Square !! style="width: 33svh" | Rectangle |- | {{Map|mtype=circle|r=18|3165,3490}} | {{Map|mtype=square|r=5.5|2253,2925}} | {{Map|mtype=rectangle|rectX=21|rectY=30|3363,3310}} |- | {{Map|mtype=circle|r=18|3165,3490|group=circle}} | {{Map|mtype=square|r=5.5|2253,2925|group=square}} | {{Map|mtype=rectangle|rectX=21|rectY=30|3363,3310|group=rectangle}} |} ===Text=== A text feature is another way to mark a precise location but with a [[#arg-text-label|label]] describing the subject. Though there are [[#Popups|configurable popups]], a text feature provides a more immediate and obvious label for something. [[#arg-text-position|position]] — Controls the placement of the text relative to the provided point. {| class="center" ! style="width: 50svh" | '''Default''' !! style="width: 50svh" | '''Right aligned''' |- | {{Map|mtype=text|2512,3466|label=Dead tree}} | {{Map|mtype=text|2802,3005|label={{fairycode|ckr}}
|position=right}} |- | {{Map|mtype=text|2512,3466|label=Dead tree|group=text}} | {{Map|mtype=text|2802,3005|label={{fairycode|ckr}}|position=right|group=text2}} |} ===RuneScape map text=== Replicates the text style seen on the in-game [[World map]]. The text's [[#arg-rstext-colour|colour]], [[#arg-rstext-weight|weight]] and [[#arg-rstext-fontSize|fontsize]] are all configurable. In cases where text is hard to read due to placement, a [[#arg-rstext-bg|background]] colour can be supplied. {| class="center" ! style="width: 33svh" | '''Default''' !! style="width: 33svh" | '''Configured''' !! style="width: 33svh" | '''Background''' |- | {{Map|mtype=rstext|label=House
on the
hill
|3779,3870}} | {{Map|mtype=rstext|label=Morytania|colour=Orange
|weight=Bold|fontsize=15pt|3500,3395} | {{Map|mtype=rstext|label=Skeletal Wyvern
|fontsize=9pt|3056,9552|background=#000000aa}} |- | {{Map|zoom=2|mtype=rstext|label=House
on the
hill|3779,3870|group=rstext}} | {{Map|zoom=0|mtype=rstext|label=Morytania|colour=Orange|weight=Bold|fontsize=15pt|3500,3395|group=rstext2}} | {{Map|mapID=-1|zoom=2|mtype=rstext|label=Skeletal Wyvern|fontsize=9pt|3056,9552|background=#000000aa|group=textground}} |- |} ===Media=== Inserts a wiki image into the map at a specific point by supplying the filename with [[#arg-media-img|img]]. Images are rendered at native size by default, which can be overriden with a custom [[#arg-media-size|size]] in pixels. For cases where images lack visiblity, an outline can be supplied with [[#arg-media-outlineColour|outlineColour]], [[#arg-media-outlineSize|outlineSize]] and [[#arg-media-outlineBlur|outlineBlur]]. {| class="center" ! style="width: 33svh" | '''Default''' !! style="width: 33svh" | '''Size''' !! style="width: 33svh" | '''Outline''' |- | {{Map|mtype=media|img=you are here.gif|2230,3178}} | {{Map|mtype=media|img=Rock_(2025_Easter_event).png
|size=60px|3325,3305}} | {{Map|mtype=media|img=Hornless_unicorn_prancing.gif
|outlineColour=red|size=50px|1630,4006}} |- | {{Map|mtype=media|img=you are here.gif|2230,3178|group=media}} | {{Map|zoom=3|mtype=media|img=Rock_(2025_Easter_event).png|size=60px|3325,3305|group=media2}} | {{Map|mtype=media|img=Hornless_unicorn_prancing.gif|size=50px|outlineColour=red|1630,4006|group=popup2}} |- |} ==Multi-point== ===Lines and polygons=== Lines and polygons are defined with a series of coordinates. Unlike lines, polygons are automatically closed — i.e., the start and end points are attached. Each point of a line is '''centered''' on its respective tile because lines should represent points that a player can stand on. Polygons, however, have points aligned to the '''south-west corner''' of their respective tile, allowing map locations to be outlined exactly. {| class="center" ! style="width: 50svh" | Line !! style="width: 50svh" | Polygon |- | {{Map|mtype=line|2728,3349|2726,3347|2722,3347 ... }} | {{Map|mtype=polygon|2721,3387|2719,3385|2719,3364 ... }} |- |{{Map|mtype=line|2728,3349|2726,3347|2722,3347|2721,3346|2712,3346|2710,3344|2710,3342|2709,3341|2707,3341|2704,3338|2704,3337|2703,3336|2703,3334|2699,3330|2699,3328|group=line}} |{{Map|mtype=polygon|2721,3387|2719,3385|2719,3364|2721,3362|2726,3362|2726,3350|2732,3350|2732,3362|2737,3362|2739,3364|2739,3385|2737,3387|group=polygon}} |- |} ===Highlighted and focused areas=== Highlighted areas are useful for emphasizing a location, de-emphasizing the surrounding area, and keep the location's contents visible. Focused areas extend this by completely blacking out the surrounding area; this can be especially useful for hiding unrelated map locations when mapID is -1. These feature types otherwise have the same functionality as polygons. {| class="center" ! style="width: 50svh" | Highlighted area !! style="width: 50svh" | Focused area |- | {{Map|mtype=highlightedarea|2557,3334|2557,3265
|2511,3265| ... }} | {{Map|mapID=-1|mtype=focusarea|3039,4850|3055.5,4842
|3055.5,4822| ... }} |- |{{Map|mtype=highlightedarea|2557,3334|2557,3265|2511,3265|2511,3280|2461,3280|2461,3306|2434,3306|2434,3322|2464,3322|2464,3334|group=highlight}} |{{Map|mapID=-1|mtype=focusarea|3039,4850|3055.5,4842|3055.5,4822|3040,4814|3022,4822|3022,4839|group=focus}} |} ==Combos== Combo features are a combination of a [[#def-single-point-feature|single-point feature]] and a [[#def-multi-point-feature|multi-point feature]]. One example is pin-line, where pin is the single-point feature and line is the multi-point feature. Combos will generate a single-point feature per coordinate and a multi-point feature using all coordinates together. {| class="center" ! style="width: 50svh" | Pins and polygon !! style="width: 50svh" | Dots and line |- | 
{{Map|mtype=rstext-highlightedarea
|2774,3469,label:text1
|2784,3459,label:text2
|2794,3469,label:text3
|2784,3479,label:text4}}
| 
{{Map|mtype=pin-line 
|2764,3468,icon:redPin
|2764,3461,icon:yellowPin
|2771,3458,icon:greenPin
|2773,3452,icon:bluePin}}
|- | {{Map|zoom=3|mtype=rstext-highlightedarea|group=combo1 |2774,3469,label:text1 |2784,3459,label:text2 |2794,3469,label:text3 |2784,3479,label:text4}} | {{Map|zoom=3|mtype=pin-line|group=combo2 |2764,3468,icon:redPin |2764,3461,icon:yellowPin |2771,3458,icon:greenPin |2773,3452,icon:bluePin}} |} Combos should be used sparingly and only when multiple coordinates have some kind of relationship. A good example is the map of tasks throughout [[One Small Favour#Walkthrough|One Small Favour]], where the tasks must be completed in a specific order. Another example is the map of [[Canoe Station|canoe stations]], where each station represents a point along the River Lum. Note that using a highlighted or focused area as the multi-point feature will inherently make all other features appear highlighted or focused as well. ==Properties== ===Colour, opacity and stroke width=== The stroke and fill of any features that have them can be changed with [[#arg-feat-stroke|stroke]] and [[#arg-feat-fill|fill]] using hex colour code values. The opacity of these are controlled with [[#arg-feat-strokeOpacity|stroke-opacity]] and [[#arg-feat-fillOpacity|fill-opacity]], where 0 is transparent and 1 is opaque. Stroke widths are controlled with [[#arg-feat-strokeWidth|stroke-width]] in pixels. {| class="center" ! style="width: 50svh" | Yellow rectangle !! style="width: 50svh" | Thin red line |- | {{Map|zoom=3|mtype=rectangle|rectX=6|rectY=8|fill=#f0ff00
|stroke-opacity=0.6|stroke=#F6B845|stroke-width=5|1883,33161}} | {{Map|mtype=line|stroke=#FF0000|stroke-width=1.5
|2912,3213|2888,3213|2888,3321|2843,3321}} |- |{{Map|zoom=3|mtype=rectangle|rectX=6|rectY=8|fill=#f0ff00|stroke-opacity=0.6|stroke=#F6B845|stroke-width=5|1883,3316|group=circle23}} |{{Map|mtype=line|stroke=#FF0000|stroke-width=1.5|2912,3213|2888,3213|2888,3321|2843,3321|group=ehbfuksdbf}} |- |} ===Offset and rotation=== [[#arg-feat-offsetX|offsetX]], [[#arg-feat-offsetY|offsetY]] — Shifts rstext and media away from the placed centre point. Positive values correspond to rightward/downward shift. [[#arg-feat-rotate|rotate]] — Rotates rstext and media. Positive values correspond to clockwise rotation. Units can be deg, rad or turn. {| class="center" ! style="width: 50svh" | '''Offset''' !! style="width: 50svh" | '''Rotate''' |- | {{Map|mtype=rstext|label=72 Agility|color=#ffff00
|offsetX=58px|fontsize=9pt|3545.8,3282}} | {{Map|zoom=3|2249.5,3458|mtype=media
|img=Map icon - Skiff.png|rotate=90deg}} |- | {{Map|mtype=rstext|zoom=2|label=72 Agility|color=#ffff00|offsetX=58px|fontsize=9pt|3545.8,3282|group=rstext44}} | {{Map|mtype=media|zoom=3|img=Map icon - Skiff.png|rotate=90deg|2249.5,3458|group=media42333}} |- |} ===Custom CSS=== Supply custom CSS with [[#arg-feat-css|css]] for either rstext or media. {| class="center" ! '''Custom css''' |- | |css=padding:1px 2px;background:#5C5041;border-radius:2.5px;border-style: outset;
border-width: 2.5px;border-color:#5C5041; outline: 1px solid black; |- | {{Map|mtype=rstext|x=1503|y=10085|mapID=-1|zoom=2|group=rstext44|label=Yama's Domain |css=padding:1px 2px;background:#5C5041;border-radius:2.5px;border-style: outset;border-width: 2.5px;border-color:#5C5041; outline: 1px solid black;|1503,10115}} |- |} ===Popups=== By default, all features are clickable to show their X/Y coordinates. For [[#def-multi-point-feature|multi-point features]], this coordinate is the first coordinate provided. However, more details can be added. * Add a title with [[#arg-popup-title|title]]. * Add a description with [[#arg-popup-desc|desc]]. {| class="center" ! style="width: 50svh" | Title !! style="width: 50svh" | Description |- | {{Map|mtype=pin|2638,3300|2661,3308|title=[[Mos Le'Water]]}} | {{Map|mtype=media|2571,3909|img=Macaroni Penguin.png
|size=28px|desc=[[Macaroni Penguin]]}} |- | {{Map|zoom=1|mtype=rstext|3901,2974|label=Mos
Le'Water|title=[[Mos Le'Water]]|group=popup1}} | {{Map|mtype=media|2571,3912|img=Macaroni Penguin.png|size=28px|desc=[[Macaroni Penguin]]|group=media2333}} |} * Add '''detailed info''' with [[#arg-popup-ptype|ptype]] if the feature represents an item, monster, object or npc. ** For any ptype, the subject's name will default to the current page's title. Set [[#arg-popup-name|name]] to change this. Specify the subject's internal ID with [[#arg-popup-id|id]] if needed. ** For monsters and NPCs, set [[#arg-popup-levels|levels]] and [[#arg-popup-respawn|respawn]] time if needed. ** For items, set [[#arg-popup-qty|qty]] and respawn time if needed. {| class="center" ! style="width: 50svh" | '''Item''' !! style="width: 50svh" | '''Monster''' |- | {{Map|mtype=pin|1275,3745|title=[[Twisted bow]]
|ptype=item|respawn=100|qty=1|name=Twisted bow|id=20997}} | {{Map|mtype=polygon|plane=1|ptype=monster
|title=[[Grid_Master#Trivia|Swarm the tower, my brethren]]|name=Lessor Demon
|id=2005|level=82|respawn=0|3110,3160|3116,3160|3116,3158 ... }} |- | {{Map|mtype=pin|1275,3745|ptype=item|title=[[Twisted bow]]|name=Twisted bow|respawn=100|qty=1|id=20997|group=item}} | {{Map|mtype=polygon|plane=1|ptype=monster|title=[[Grid_Master#Trivia|Swarm the tower, my brethren]]|name=Lessor Demon|id=2005|level=82|respawn=0|3110,3160|3116,3160|3116,3158|3112,3154|3107,3154|3103,3158|3103,3159|3110,3159|group=npc}} |} ===Grouping=== [[#arg-feat-group|group]] is used to set custom feature grouping. By default, all features belong to the same group and will therefore appear on every map on a page. {| class="center" ! style="width: 33svh" | Lone group !! style="width: 33svh" | Grouped with [[#Circles,_squares_and_rectangles|circles]] |- | {{Map|x=3165|y=3494|group=alone}} | {{Map|x=3165|y=3494|group=circle} |- | {{Map|x=3165|y=3494|group=alone}} | {{Map|x=3165|y=3494|group=circle}} |} =Advanced usage= ===Anonymous features=== Multiple map features can be defined through [[#def-anonymous-feature|anonymous features]], which have the general form: |option1:value1,optionN:valueN,x1:y1,xN:yN You can provide as many options and coordinates as you want for a single anonymous feature. Each option/value and x/y must be separated by a colon (:), and each of these pairings must be separated by a comma (,). The options available to use in anonymous features are exactly the same as regular [[#Feature options|named arguments]], meaning the two are entirely interchangeable. If a named argument is also provided as an anonymous argument, the anonymous value will override the named value. One small difference with anonymous features—because they are comma- and colon-separated—is the need to escape ''extra'' commas and colons with \ backslashes in certain options. These are mentioned in the table of [[#Feature options|feature options]] below. {| class="center" |- | |mtype:rstext,3211:3247,label:A comma \,
and a colon \:
|mtype:pin,3246:3248,desc:A comma \,
and a colon \: |- |{{Map|mtype:rstext,3211:3247,label:A comma \,
and a colon \: |mtype:pin,3246:3248,desc:A comma \,
and a colon \:|group=anonfeats}} |} Because the anonymous feature syntax is used solely to create features, [[#Map options|map-only options]] cannot be used as feature options. ===Transclusion=== Many maps that contain a large number of features (or are otherwise complex and lengthy) are sometimes defined on their own under the [https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Special:PrefixIndex?namespace=118 Map] namespace and then [https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Transclusion transcluded] in another page. {| |- | {{Map:Multicombat AGT}} |- | {{Map:Multicombat AGT}} |} ===Bucket=== By default the Map module provides functionality that allows other pages, templates, and modules to interact with its data. More specifically, the final map options and GeoJSON for each feature will be stored in bucket for other resources to consume. See [[Bucket:Map]] for example data. In some cases, a page will have multiple maps that relate to specific instances of the page's subject. For example, [[Forestry Shop]] has three maps that each relate to one of its locations. To handle this, you can set bucketName to tell the Map module to store each map in a separate Bucket entry under the page; Otherwise, each of the maps would overwrite each other. The value of bucketName should match the subject's instance name if possible ("Draynor Village", "Seers' Village", or "Prifddinas" in the Forestry Shop example). =Arguments= ==Map options== Map options are [[#def-named-argument|named arguments]] that define how the map itself behaves and how it is rendered on the page. These options cannot be used as feature options. {{ArgDocHeader}} {{ArgDocLine |name = type |description = Sets the map type on the page. |values = mapframe maplink |default = mapframe |id = map-type }} {{ArgDocLine |name = width |description = Sets the map width on the page. |values = Any number >=1 |default = 300 |id = map-width }} {{ArgDocLine |name = height |description = Sets the map height on the page. |values = Any number >=1 |default = 300 |id = map-height }} {{ArgDocLine |name = align |description = Sets the map's alignment on the page. |values = left center right |default = center |id = align }} {{ArgDocLine |name = x |description = Sets the X coordinate of the map view if at least one feature is defined. |values = Any number >=0 |default = 3233 |id = map-x }} {{ArgDocLine |name = y |description = Sets the Y coordinate of the map view if at least one feature is defined. |values = Any number >=0 |default = 3222 |id = map-y }} {{ArgDocLine |name = zoom |description = Sets the zoom amount. A higher number means a closer zoom. |values = Any integer -3–5 |default = 2 |id = map-zoom }} {{ArgDocLine |name = mapID |description = Sets the map ID. |values = Any [[RuneScape:Map/mapIDs|map ID]] |default = 0 |id = map-mapid }} {{ArgDocLine |name = caption |description = Adds a caption to the map if type is unset or set to mapframe. |values = Any text |id = map-caption }} {{ArgDocLine |name = text |description = If type is set to maplink, changes the text of the link. |values = Any text |id = map-text }} {{ArgDocLine |name = nopreprocess |description = Outputs the final map element with GeoJSON as raw text instead of a rendered map. |values = True }} {{ArgDocFooter}} ==Feature options== Feature options are [[#def-named-argument|named]] or [[#def-anonymous-argument|anonymous]] arguments that define features on the map. {{ArgDocHeader}} {{ArgDocLine |name = mtype |description = Sets the type of a feature. |values = pin rectangle square circle dot text rstext media line polygon highlightedarea focusarea or a [[#def-combo-feature|combo type]] |default = pin |id = feat-mtype }} {{ArgDocLine |name = x |description = Sets the X coordinate of a feature. Can also be set with [[#def-coordinate-shorthand|coordinate shorthand]]. |values = Any number >=0 |default = 3233 }} {{ArgDocLine |name = y |description = Sets the Y coordinate of a feature. Can also be set with [[#def-coordinate-shorthand|coordinate shorthand]]. |values = Any number >=0 |default = 3222 }} {{ArgDocLine |name = plane |description = Sets the plane (Z value) a feature is on. |values = Any integer 0–3 |default = 0 |id = feat-plane }} {{ArgDocLine |name = stroke |description = Sets the stroke color of a feature with a stroke. |values = Any hexadecimal color code |default = #3388ff |id = feat-stroke }} {{ArgDocLine |name = stroke-opacity |description = Sets the stroke opacity of a feature with a stroke. |values = Any number 0–1 |default = 1 |id = feat-strokeOpacity }} {{ArgDocLine |name = stroke-width |description = Sets the stroke width of a feature with a stroke. |values = Any number >=0 |default = 3 |id = feat-strokeWidth }} {{ArgDocLine |name = fill |description = Sets the fill color of a feature with a fill. |values = Any hexadecimal color code |default = #3388ff |id = feat-fill }} {{ArgDocLine |name = fill-opacity |description = Sets the fill opacity of a feature with a fill. |values = Any number 0–1 |default = 0.2 |id = feat-fillOpacity }} {{ArgDocLine |name = group |description = Sets the group for a feature. Features on separate map instances will appear on all instances on the same page if the group name is the same. Consider adding a unique group name if a page has a lot of pins. |values = Any text |default = pins |id = feat-group }} {{ArgDocLine |description = Any number of anonymous features. |values = See [[#Anonymous features|Anonymous features]] }} {{ArgDocFooter}} {{ArgDocHeader|caption=Popups}} {{ArgDocLine |name = title |description = Sets the popup title of a feature. In an [[#Anonymous features|anonymous feature]], all commas and colons within must be escaped with \ backslashes. |values = Any text |id = popup-title }} {{ArgDocLine |name = desc |description = Sets the popup description of a feature. In an [[#Anonymous features|anonymous feature]], all commas and colons within must be escaped with \ backslashes. |values = Any text |id = popup-desc }} {{ArgDocLine |name = ptype |description = Sets the feature's subject's type for providing extra popup details. |values = item monster npc object |id = popup-ptype }} {{ArgDocLine |name = name |description = Sets the feature's subject's name if ptype is set. |values = Any text |default = The page's title |id = popup-name }} {{ArgDocLine |name = id |description = Adds the feature's subject's internal ID to the popup if ptype is set. |values = Any integer |id = popup-id }} {{ArgDocLine |name = qty |description = Adds the feature's subject's quantity to the popup if ptype is set to item. |values = Any integer |id = popup-qty }} {{ArgDocLine |name = respawn |description = Adds the feature's subject's respawn time to the popup if ptype is set to item, npc, or monster. |values = Any text |id = popup-respawn }} {{ArgDocLine |name = levels |description = Adds the feature's subject's list of levels to the popup if ptype is set to monster or npc. |values = Any text |id = popup-levels }} {{ArgDocFooter}} {{ArgDocHeader|caption=Circles and squares}} {{ArgDocLine |name = r |description = Sets the radius of a circle or square. |values = Any number >=1 |default = 10 |id = feat-r }} {{ArgDocFooter}} {{ArgDocHeader|caption=Rectangles}} {{ArgDocLine |name = rectX |description = Sets the X length for a rectangle. |values = Any number >=1 |default = 20 |id = rect-x }} {{ArgDocLine |name = rectY |description = Sets the Y length for a rectangle. |values = Any number >=1 |default = 20 |id = rect-y }} {{ArgDocFooter}} {{ArgDocHeader|caption=Pins}} {{ArgDocLine |name = icon |description = Sets the icon for a pin feature using a built-in value. |values = greenPin redPin bluePin cyanPin magentaPin yellowPin greyPin |default = greenPin |id = pin-icon }} {{ArgDocFooter}} {{ArgDocHeader|caption=Text}} {{ArgDocLine |name = label |description = Sets the label text of a text feature. In an [[#Anonymous features|anonymous feature]], all commas and colons within must be escaped with \ backslashes. |values = Any text |required = Yes |id = text-label }} {{ArgDocLine |name = position |description = Sets the position of a text feature's label. |values = left right top bottom center |default = top |id = text-position }} {{ArgDocFooter}} {{ArgDocHeader|caption=rstext}} {{ArgDocLine |name = color
colour |description = Sets the color of an rstext feature's label. |values = Any CSS color value |default = white |id = rstext-colour }} {{ArgDocLine |name = font |description = Sets the font of an rstext feature's label. |values = Any font available on the wiki |default = Verdana }} {{ArgDocLine |name = weight |description = Sets the font weight of an rstext feature's label. |values = Any CSS font-weight value |default = normal |id = rstext-weight }} {{ArgDocLine |name = fontSize |description = Sets the font size of an rstext feature's label. |values = Any CSS font-size value |default = 11pt |id = rstext-fontSize }} {{ArgDocLine |name = background |description = Sets the background of an rstext feature's label. |values = Any CSS background value |id = rstext-bg }} {{ArgDocFooter}} {{ArgDocHeader|caption=Media}} {{ArgDocLine |name = img |description = Sets the image file of a media feature. |values = Any wiki image file name with extension |id = media-img }} {{ArgDocLine |name = size |description = Sets the size of a media feature. |values = Any pixel value with unit |default = Native size of the file |id = media-size }} {{ArgDocLine |name = outlineColour |description = Sets the colour of the outline a media feature. |values = Any CSS color value |id = media-outlineColour }} {{ArgDocLine |name = outlineSize |description = Sets the size of the outline a media feature. |values = Any CSS length value |id = media-outlineSize }} {{ArgDocLine |name = outlineBlur |description = Sets the blue of the outline a media feature. |values = Any CSS length value |id = media-outlineBlur }} {{ArgDocFooter}} {{ArgDocHeader|caption=rstext and media}} {{ArgDocLine |name = offsetX |description = Offsets a feature horizontally. Positive values correspond to rightward shift. |values = Any CSS length value |id = feat-offsetX }} {{ArgDocLine |name = offsetY |description = Offsets a feature vertically. Positive values correspond to downward shift. |values = Any CSS length value |id = feat-offsetY }} {{ArgDocLine |name = rotate |description = Rotates a feature. Positive values correspond to clockwise rotation. |values = Any CSS angle value (with units) |id = feat-rotate }} {{ArgDocLine |name = css |description = Adds custom CSS properties to the style of a feature. |values = Any CSS properties |id = feat-css }} {{ArgDocFooter}} ==Bucket options== {{ArgDocHeader}} {{ArgDocLine |name = bucket |description = Enables [[Bucket:Map|Bucket data]] for the current page. This should only be used if the map directly relates to the page subject. See [[#Bucket|Bucket]] for more info. |values = yes hist both |default = yes }} {{ArgDocLine |name = bucketName |description = A subpage name used to store a specific instance of a page in Bucket. This should only be used if the map does ''not'' directly describe the page subject. See [[#Bucket|Bucket]] for more info. |values = Any subpage name }} {{ArgDocLine |name = fromBucket |description = A page or subpage name to pull from [[Bucket:Map|Bucket]] and build a fully rendered map. No provided feature options will be processed. Any provided map options will combine with or override the page's map options. |values = Any page or subpage name }} {{ArgDocFooter}} =Definitions= *
'''Named argument''' - An argument with the form |arg=value. **
'''Named feature''' - A feature defined entirely with named arguments. *
'''Anonymous argument''' - An argument with the form |value. **
'''Anonymous feature''' - A feature defined entirely or partially with anonymous arguments. Uses the format |option1:value1,optionN:valueN,x1:y1,xN:yN. *
'''Single-point feature''' - A feature defined by a single point. ** pin, rectangle, square, circle, dot, text, rstext, media *
'''Multi-point feature''' - A feature defined by multiple points. ** line, polygon, highlightedarea, focusarea *
'''Combo feature''' - A feature that combines a ''single-point'' feature with a ''multi-point'' feature. Examples: pin-line, dot-line, and pin-polygon. *
'''Coordinate shorthand''' - A more compact way to provide X/Y coordinates for a feature. Allows multiple coordinates to be provided. ** For ''named features'', this could look like |1000,1000|2000,2000. ** For ''anonymous features'', this could look like |1000:1000,2000:2000. =Cleanup tasks= * Many uses of this template still use squareX and squareY to define both squares and rectangles. These options are still supported in the code only as a backwards compatibility measure. Any uses of these should be changed to rectX and rectY respectively. ** If these numbers '''do''' match, switch these options out with r and ensure the mtype is square. ** If these numbers '''don't''' match, the mtype should be changed to rectangle. =See also= * [[Module:Map/doc|Map module API]] * [[User:Als Toy Barn/Map|Map template test suite]]

revision.text:
local p = {}
local styles = { w = 'width:1%;', ws = 'white-space:pre;', bgc = 'background-color:var(--wikitable-header-bg);' }
function p.main(frame) local tArgs = frame:getParent().args local mArgs = {} local mArgNames = {} local argCount = 0
if not tArgs.funcName then error('APIDoc requires `funcName` argument', 0) end
while tArgs['arg'..(argCount + 1)] do argCount = argCount + 1 end
for i = 1, argCount do table.insert(mArgNames, tArgs['arg'..i]) table.insert(mArgs, { name = tArgs['arg'..i], type = tArgs['type'..i], desc = tArgs['desc'..i], optional = tArgs['optional'..i] }) end
local tableElem = mw.html.create('table'):addClass('wikitable') local argList = table.concat(mArgNames, ', ')
tableElem:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('colspan', '4') :tag('code') :wikitext(string.format('%s(%s)', tArgs.funcName, argList or ''))
tableElem:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('colspan', '4') :wikitext(tArgs.funcDesc)
if #mArgs > 0 or tArgs.returnType then local row = tableElem:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('style', styles.w..styles.bgc) :wikitext((#mArgs > 0 and "'''Argument'''") or '') :tag('td') :attr('style', styles.w..styles.bgc) :wikitext("'''Type'''") :tag('td') :attr('style', styles.bgc) :wikitext("'''Description'''")
if #mArgs > 0 then row:tag('td') :attr('style', styles.w..styles.bgc) :wikitext("'''Optional'''") end end
for _, mArg in ipairs(mArgs) do tableElem:tag('tr') :tag('td'):wikitext(mArg.name) :tag('td') :attr('style', styles.ws) :wikitext(mArg.type) :tag('td'):wikitext(mArg.desc) :tag('td'):wikitext(mArg.optional and '[[File:Yes_check.svg|15px|center]]') end
local returnTypeElem = mw.html.create('td') local returnDescElem = mw.html.create('td')
if tArgs.returnType then returnTypeElem :attr('style', styles.w) :wikitext(tArgs.returnType)
if tArgs.returnDesc then returnDescElem :attr('colspan', '2') :wikitext(tArgs.returnDesc) end else returnTypeElem :attr('style', styles.w..styles.ws..styles.bgc) :addClass('table-na') :wikitext('--') returnDescElem :attr('style', styles.bgc) :attr('colspan', '2') :addClass('table-na') end
tableElem:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('style', styles.w..styles.bgc) :addClass('table-na') :wikitext('Returns') :node(returnTypeElem) :node(returnDescElem)
return tableElem end
return p

revision.text:
{{documentation}} {{invokes|Mmgtable}} This template displays an infobox for a money making guide. ==Usage== This template can be used by entering the following onto a relevant page. It will automatically add [[:Category:Money making guides]] to the page. 
{{Mmgtable
|Define variables =
|Activity =
|Image =
|Skill =
|Item =
|Quest =
|Other =
|Other Benefits =
|Input# =
|Input#num =
|Input#value =
|Input#note =
|Output# =
|Output#num =
|Output#value =
|Output#note =
|Location =
|Category =
|Members =
|Intensity =
|Details =
|kph = 
|kph name = 
|isperkill = 
}}
==Define variables== Define your {{#Vardefine:}} variables here to make sure they are available for the other parameters. ==Activity== This parameter states the activity to make money. ==Version== Only required when utilising a Tabber to have multiple mmgtables on one page.
This should be set to the same as the tabber title to ensure it can auto-switch to the correct table. This also appears in the main table on [[money making guide]] in brackets. ==Image== This parameter displays an image. ==Skill== This parameter states the skill requirements for the activity. ==Item== This parameter states the items needed for the activity. ==Quest== This parameter states the quests that need to be done for the activity. ==Other== This parameter lists other requirements not covered by the Skill, Item and Quest parameters. ==Other Benefits== This parameter lists any experience rewards or other non-monetary benefits of this method. ==Input#, Input#num, Input#value, Input#note, Input#isph== These parameters state the inputs needed to start the activity. The # is replaced with a whole, positive number, in sequence, starting from 1. * Input# specifies the item. * Input#num specifies how many of the item will be used per hour. * Input#value specifies the per-item value of the item (if it's different from the Grand Exchange price). * Input#note can be used to specify other information about an input, such as stating that a coin cost represents expenses related to repairing equipment. * Input#isph can be used to specify that the input is required per hour. Default is true. If set to false, the input number will be multiplied by kph. ==Output#, Output#num, Output#value, and Output#note== These parameters state the outputs received from the activity. The # is replaced with a whole, positive number, in sequence, starting from 1. * Output# specifies the item. * Output#num specifies how many of the item will be obtained per hour. * Output#value specifies the per-item value of the item (if it's different from the Grand Exchange price). * Output#note can specify other information about an output, such as stating that a coin output is the result of using High level alchemy. ==Location== This parameter states the location of the activity. Currently, this is not actually displayed anywhere. ==Category== This parameter states whether the activity is: "Combat", "Collecting", "Skilling", or "Processing". "Combat/Low", "Combat/Mid", and "Combat/High" also work for "Combat", if more specific categorization is desired. ==Members== This parameter states whether the activity is Free-to-play ("Members=No"). If this parameter is not set, the page will be added to [[:Category:Money making guides without a membership status]]. ==Intensity== This parameter states whether the activity is:"High", "Moderate" or "Low" intensity.
Should no argument be given or if the argument is invalid, it will default to "Unknown". ==Details== This parameter lists details for the activity. ==kph== This parameter allows you to specify a number of kills or actions per hour. This is to be used with Input#isph and isperkill to allow the user to customize their actions per hour. ==kph name== This parameter specifies the name of the "kills per hour" (default) label, for money making guides that are not based on kills. ==isperkill== This parameter specifies whether the outputs are given per-kill rather than per-hour. ==Exclude== Set to yes to prevent the template from writing to Bucket, which will prevent it showing up in the MMG lists. It also adds [[:Category:Obsolete money making guides]]. ==Deprecated parameters== The following parameters are still usable, but should not be used. ===Inputs=== A formatted list of all inputs. Should be replaced with the Input# parameters. ===Outputs=== A formatted list of all outputs. Should be replaced with the Output# parameters. ===Profit=== The expected hourly profit. If Inputs and Outputs have been properly replaced, this will be automatically calculated, and this parameter should be removed. [[Category:Table templates]]

{{Documentation}} This template displays a standard table for money making guide tables. ==Usage== This template can be used by entering the following onto a money making table. 
{{Mmgtable recurring
|Activity = 
|Image = 
|Activity Time = 
|Recurrence Time = 
|Skill = 
|Item =
|Quest =
|Other =
|Other Benefits =
|Input# =
|Input#num =
|Input#value =
|Input#note =
|Output# =
|Output#num =
|Output#value =
|Output#note =
|Location =
|Category =
|Members =
|Intensity =
|Details =
}}
==Activity== This parameter states the activity to make money. ==Version== Only required when utilising a Tabber to have multiple mmgtables on one page. This should be set to the same as the tabber title to ensure it can auto-switch to the correct table. This also appears in the main table on [[money making guide]] in parenthesis. ==Image== This parameter displays an image. ==Activity time== Time to perform the activity, in minutes ==Recurrence time== How much time needs to pass before the activity can be performed again. Include the time unit (eg |Recurrence time = 1440 minutes). ==Skill== This parameter states the skill requirements for the activity. ==Item== This parameter states the items needed for the activity. ==Quest== This parameter states the quests that need to be done for the activity. ==Other== This parameter lists other requirements not covered by the Skill, Item and Quest parameters. ==Other Benefits== This parameter lists any experience rewards or other non-monetary benefits of this method. ==Input#, Input#num, Input#value, and Input#note== These parameters state the inputs needed to start the activity. The # is replaced with a number. Input#num specifies how many of the item will be used per hour. Input#value specifies the per-item value of the item (if it's different from the Grand Exchange price). Input#note can be used to specify other information about an input, such as stating that a coin cost represents expenses related to repairing equipment. ==Output#, Output#num, Output#value, and Output#note== These parameters state the outputs received from the activity. The # is replaced with a number. Input#num specifies how many of the item will be used per hour. Input#value specifies the per-item value of the item (if it's different from the Grand Exchange price). Output#note can specify other information about an output, such as stating that a coin output is the result of using High level alchemy. ==Location== This parameter states the location of the activity. ==Category== This parameter states whether the activity is: "Combat", "Collecting", "Skilling", or "Processing". ==Members== This parameter states whether the activity is Free-to-play("members=No").
Note: this parameter is not required if the activity requires membership. ==Intensity== This parameter states whether the activity is:"High", "Moderate" or "Low" intensity.
Should no argument be given or if the argument is invalid, it will default to "Unknown". ==Details== This parameter lists details for the activity. ==Exclude== Set to yes to prevent the template from writing to Bucket, which will prevent it showing up in the MMG lists. It also adds [[:Category:Obsolete money making guides]]. ==Deprecated parameters== The following parameters are still usable, but should not be used. ===Inputs=== A formatted list of all inputs. revision.text:
{{documentation|Template:Navbox}} {{invokes|Navbox|category=No}} __TOC__ ==Usage== This template can be used to make a standard navigation box. It is intended for use within another template that standardises the title and contents of the box (see [[Template:Rune equipment]]). This template should not be used directly within articles, as it creates a maintenance burden to do so whenever the contents of the box have to be updated. ==Syntax== 
{{Navbox
|state = uncollapsed, collapsed, plain, autocollapse (default)
|name = mandatory - name of the template
|style = optional - style for the whole table
|title = mandatory - navbox header
|gtitleN = optional - title of N-th group of items
|styleN = optional - style for groupN; i.e. text-align
|groupN = mandatory - list of groups of items
|fstyle = optional - style for footer ; i.e. text-align
|footer = optional - navbox footer
}}
* '''Groups:''' ** Groups of items can be added as parameters: ''group1'', ''group2'', ''group3'', ... up to ''groupN''. * '''Group title:''' Each group has its own title parameter: ''gtitle1'', ''gtitle2'', ''gtitle3'', ... up to ''gtitleN''. * '''Group style:''' Style may also be customised to each group in: ''style1'', ''style2'', ''style3'', ... up to ''styleN''. * '''Superscript:''' It is preferred to use superscript () to denote variants of items that are already contained in the navbox. * '''Bullets:''' Create unordered lists with lines beginning with *. ==States== * '''Autocollapse:''' By default, the state of a navbox is "autocollapsed". This means that if the number of navboxes in a page exceeds the maximum allocation of the collapsible navboxes, then the remaining navboxes are collapsed automatically. For more information (or to change the setting), see [[MediaWiki:Gadget-autocollapse.js]]. ** Currently, the ''autocollapse'' allocation is '''2'''. This means that if there are 3 navboxes in a page, the third and subsequent navboxes will be collapsed automatically. * '''Uncollapsed:''' Forces the navbox to be displayed. * '''Collapsed:''' The reverse of ''uncollapsed''. Forces the navbox to be hidden instead. ** Navboxes with a height of more than 300 pixels will also be collapsed automatically. For more information (or to change the setting), see [[MediaWiki:Gadget-autocollapse.js]]. * '''Plain:''' Removes the "show/hide" link. ==Sub-groups== * For larger navboxes, it may be necessary to include sub-groups within a particular group of items. It is also possible to collapsible navboxes within the parent navbox, see [[#Collapsible sub-groups|Collapsible sub-groups]]. * To create sub-groups within {{Navbox}}, certain parameters are to be included: ** The parent navbox group (i.e. ''group2'' in the example below) requires the type parameter (''gtype2 = subgroup''). ** The nested navbox (sub-group) requires the inclusion of the sub-group parameter (''subgroup = yes''). This enables the template to differentiate between the sub-group and the parent navbox. 
{{Navbox
|name = 
|title = 
|gtitle1 = 
|group1 =
|gtitle2 = 
|gtype2 = subgroup (mandatory)
|group2 =
  {{Navbox
  |subgroup = yes (mandatory)
  |gtitle1 = 
  |group1 =
  |gtitle2 = 
  |group2 =
  }}
}}
==Collapsible sub-groups== * For extremely long navboxes, it is recommended to use collapsible navboxes within the parent navbox. Further sub-groups can then be added to these collapsible navboxes. * To create collapsible sub-groups within {{Navbox}}, these parameters need to be included: ** The parent navbox is almost always uncollapsed (''state=uncollapsed''). ** The parent navbox group (i.e. ''group1'' in the example below) requires the type parameter (''gtype1 = subgroup''). ** The nested collapsible navbox requires the inclusion of the collapsible parameter (''collapsible = yes''). This enables the template to differentiate between the collapsible navbox and the parent navbox. ** The nested collapsible navbox is forcefully collapsed (''state=collapsed''). 
{{Navbox
|state = uncollapsed
|name = 
|gtype1 = subgroup
|group1 = 
  {{Navbox
  |collapsible = yes
  |state = collapsed
  |title = 
  |gtitle1 = 
  |group1 =
  |gtitle2 = 
  |group2 =
  }}
}}
==Use of images== * The use of images in navboxes is permitted, but please resize the images to keep them small. Inventory-sized images (25-30 pixels) are recommended. ** Use {{t|plink}} to create links with images. ** Use {{t|plinkp}} for any case where text is not desired after the link. ** Use {{t|chatl}} to link chatheads. ** Use {{t|Emote link}} to link emote icons. * Avoid using images in the main header of the navbox. Link and file share the same name 
{{plink|Item}}
File name differs from the link 
{{plink|Item|pic=File}}
Link and file share the same name, but different text is desired to display 
{{plink|Item|txt=Text}}
File name differs from the link and different text is desired to display 
{{plink|Item|pic=File|txt=Text}}
{|class="wikitable" |+ Examples !Code !Standard syntax |- |{{plink|Abyssal whip}} |[[File:Abyssal whip.png|link=Abyssal whip]] [[Abyssal whip]] |- |{{plink|Granite maul|pic=Abyssal whip}} |[[File:Abyssal whip.png|link=Granite maul]] [[Granite maul]] |- |{{plink|Abyssal whip|txt=Whip}} |[[File:Abyssal whip.png|link=Abyssal whip]] [[Abyssal whip|Whip]] |- |{{plink|Granite maul|pic=Abyssal whip|txt=Whip}} |[[File:Abyssal whip.png|link=Granite maul]] [[Granite maul|Whip]] |- |{{plinkp|Abyssal whip}} |[[File:Abyssal whip.png|link=Abyssal whip]] |- |{{plinkp|Granite maul|pic=Abyssal whip}} |[[File:Abyssal whip.png|link=Granite maul]] |- |} ==Categorising== Navboxes are useful for transcluding categories onto a large number of pages that share both a trait and the navigation box. For example: [[Template:Rune equipment]] transcludes [[:Category:Rune]] onto every page that uses it. There are 2 methods of categorising pages with navboxes: The preferred method is to use '''{{t|Ctg}}'''. This has the most simple rules but is the easiest to use. The other method is to use '''{{t|Mainonly|rules}}''' and provide more complex rules with parser functions. [[Template:Potions]] is an example of this: 
{{mainonly|{{#ifeq:{{lc:{{#sub:{{PAGENAME}}|-3}}}}|mix|[[Category:Barbarian mixes]]}}}}
This code tells the template to add [[:Category:Barbarian mixes]] to pages only if their title ends with the string "mix". {{ctg|Barbarian mixes::ifmatches[mix]}} would '''not''' work here, because several pages include the substring "mix" in other locations, and they would be improperly categorised. Categorisation should only be used on a template for large-scale addition. For small numbers of pages it is simpler to directly add the category to each page. ==Examples== {{#ifeq:{{BASEPAGENAME}}|Navbox||To see the following navboxes in action, see [[Template:Navbox]].}} ===Single line navbox with centered list=== {{#ifeq:{{BASEPAGENAME}}|Navbox|{{Navbox |state = uncollapsed |name = Navbox |title = [[RuneScape:Sandbox|Single line navbox]] |style1 = text-align:center |group1 = * Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet * Consectetur adipisicing elit * sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua }}}}

==Preventing unwanted documentation== The [[Template:Navbox/doc|Navbox template's documentation]] is automatically transcluded under the navbox on any Template namespace page. It is not transcluded when used as a sub-group or collapsible sub-group template (''subgroup= yes'' or ''collapsible=yes''). Should the documentation appear when it is unwanted, it can be hidden by setting the doc parameter ''doc=no'' on the template. In most cases, the doc parameter is not used and the parameter is removed completely. On a similar note, the automatically-added category [[:Category:Navbox templates]] can be suppressed by adding ''hidecat=yes''. {{documentation}} :''Not to be confused with [[Template:Old School RuneScape Wiki/Poll]]'' This template provides formatting for poll results for use in Old School Content Poll pages. This automatically ignores answer votes for percentage calculation for answers with the names Skip question and Skip. ==Usage== This template can be used by entering the following code. 
{{Poll
|Question   <-- The question text on the poll -->
|AnswerX    <-- The answer text on the poll -->
|VotesX     <-- The number of votes for an answer -->
|Note       <-- Additional notes for the question -->
}}
For example: 
{{Poll|Question=Do you want to understand this template?|Answer1=Yes|Votes1=8000|Answer2=No|Votes2=2000}}
{{Poll|Question=Do you want to understand this template?|Answer1=Yes|Votes1=8000|Answer2=No|Votes2=2000}} For more answers: 
{{Poll|Question=Do you want to add more answers?|Answer1=Yes|Votes1=8000|Answer2=No|Votes2=1500|Answer3=Skip question|Votes3=500}}
{{Poll|Question=Do you want to add more answers?|Answer1=Yes|Votes1=8000|Answer2=No|Votes2=1500|Answer3=Skip question|Votes3=500}} This template currently supports up to 20 answers per question. For a note: 
{{Poll|Question=Do you want to add a note?|Answer1=Yes|Votes1=8000|Answer2=From time to time|Votes2=8000|Answer3=Occasionally|Votes3=8000|Note=This is a multiple-choice question.}}
{{Poll|Question=Do you want to add a note?|Answer1=Yes|Votes1=8000|Answer2=From time to time|Votes2=8000|Answer3=Occasionally|Votes3=8000|Note=This is a multiple-choice question.}} [[Category:Formatting templates|{{PAGENAME}}]]

{{documentation}} {{Confuse|Template:Poll|Template:Old School RuneScape Wiki/Poll}} This template provides formatting for poll results for use in transciption of the ''[[RuneScape]]'' website [https://secure.runescape.com/m=poll/archive poll archive]. This explicitly '''includes''' "Skip" votes in overall vote percentage calculation, as is reflected in the archive. ==Usage== This template can be used by entering the following code: 
{{PollArchive
|Question   
|AnswerX    
|VotesX     
|Note       
}}
For example: 
{{PollArchive|Question=Do you want to understand this template?|Answer1=Yes|Votes1=8000|Answer2=No|Votes2=2000}}
{{PollArchive|Question=Do you want to understand this template?|Answer1=Yes|Votes1=8000|Answer2=No|Votes2=2000}} For more answers: 
{{PollArchive|Question=Do you want to add more answers?|Answer1=Yes|Votes1=8000|Answer2=No|Votes2=1500|Answer3=Skip question|Votes3=500}}
{{PollArchive|Question=Do you want to add more answers?|Answer1=Yes|Votes1=8000|Answer2=No|Votes2=1500|Answer3=Skip question|Votes3=500}} This template currently supports up to 20 answers per question. For a note: 
{{PollArchive|Question=Do you want to add a note?|Answer1=Yes|Votes1=8000|Answer2=From time to time|Votes2=8000|Answer3=Occasionally|Votes3=8000|Note=This is a multiple-choice question.}}
{{PollArchive|Question=Do you want to add a note?|Answer1=Yes|Votes1=8000|Answer2=From time to time|Votes2=8000|Answer3=Occasionally|Votes3=8000|Note=This is a multiple-choice question.}} ==See also== * [[Template:PollWrapper]] [[Category:Formatting templates|{{PAGENAME}}]]
